gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the false all-H^1 initial-guess/contraction claim: the correction operator preserves nonhomogeneous Dirichlet trace, so the approximation estimate cannot be applied and an explicit nonzero-trace initial error persists.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The iteration and its contraction proof are asserted for arbitrary H^1 initial data even though the exact-solution and correction spaces impose homogeneous Dirichlet trace; corrections cannot remove an initial trace mismatch.

component_coverage.gold_component: The exact and correction constructions lie in the homogeneous Dirichlet space, so an initial guess outside that space retains its nonzero boundary trace.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-009 explicitly states that every correction has zero Dirichlet trace and that the homogeneous-boundary approximation estimate cannot be applied to arbitrary H^1 functions.

component_coverage.gold_component: The stated contraction and convergence guarantee fail for such initial data, as shown by a persistent positive-energy error.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-009 supplies the same harmonic nonzero-trace example and states that the iteration remains unchanged with positive energy error regardless of coarse-space size.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-008 concerns the prefactor and global-versus-local norm used after a valid local estimate. It does not identify the distinct quantifier error of promoting a solution-specific approximation estimate to an operator bound for every admissible v, nor the required reapplication with F_v.

ISSUE-012 diagnoses an incorrect velocity-field interpretation in a numerical experiment. It does not recognize that the partition of unity is left nonunique, causing different generalized eigenvectors, coarse spaces, preconditioners, and unreconstructible reported outputs.

ISSUE-012 concerns the sign and interpretation of the specified velocity field. It does not identify the omitted source f in the 3D PDE or the resulting nonuniqueness of the right-hand side, residual history, and iteration count.
